spec: S-12 §7.1 (contract/library-v2/SPEC.md): deleted meetings in .cassini/trash/, journaled moves, restore names, purge, and crash recovery. HARMONY §7.1 has the UX.
howToRead: Start from input.files (+ input.dirs), apply input.before fully (op ids op-01, op-02...), add input.putAfterBefore, then run input.request as op-1. expected.steps is the planned step list (journal write first, retirement last). crashMatrix[k] stops after step k, runs startup recovery, and gives the resulting state: k = 0 is the untouched state; every k >= 1 rolls forward to expected.after. Entry and op ids are fixed here; apps use fresh UUIDs.

cases.note: Published file whose working folder was already cleaned up: the file moves into the entry; it leaves the Library list, Search and Export at once.
Imported standalone Cassini file without our x (identity = audio digest).
Restore (or Undo): the original name is free, so the file returns under it, byte-identical.
Another meeting now has the original name: §2 suffix from the stored prefix and title.
The occupant differs only by case: still taken (casefold key), so (2).
Base and (2) are taken: (3).
A file without a persisted prefix: the original stem takes the suffix.
The original file was copied back into the Library by hand (same session identity, original name): Restore is refused before anything moves (trash.restoreFailed).

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: A copy under another name still has the same session identity: refused.

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: A standalone file without our x was copied back under another name: the audio digest matches, so Restore is refused.

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: A published-only entry whose session is live again as an unpublished working folder: refused.

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: Delete permanently: the entry is renamed to .purge-<id>, then removed; nothing reaches the system Trash.
Published file and working folder move into one entry, the file first (it is what the Library lists).
Both return together: the working folder first, then the file, so the row reappears complete.
The file takes a §2 suffix; the folder returns under its own identity.
The same session is live again: Restore is refused before anything moves (trash.restoreFailed).

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: Only the published file was copied back by hand (no working folder): the identity is live in a root file, so Restore is refused.

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: The published file and its working folder are both live again: refused.

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: Both representations are removed.
A hand-made copy of the published file is also live: only the chosen file moves; the working folder stays with the copy that stays in the Library.
Restoring that entry while the copy is still live is refused.

expected.reason: a meeting with this identity is already in the Library

cases.note: An interrupted (unpublished) v2 meeting: only its working folder moves.
A live activity lease (Recording/Saving): refused, nothing changes.

expected.reason: recording or saving holds the activity lease

cases.note: A working folder whose identity is also in a live published file is not a lone unpublished meeting: Move of the folder alone is refused (move the published row).

expected.reason: a published file with this identity is still in the Library

cases.note: It returns to .cassini/sessions/ and is listed as before.
Its folder is removed.
A v1 Library (LIBRARY-RULES R1): the root meeting folder moves; .cassini/ is created if needed and is invisible to v1 scanners.
It returns to the root under its own name; §8 conversion then treats it like any v1 folder.
Its folder is removed.
Empty Trash / Delete All: one purge (and one journal entry) per entry, newest deletion first.
